what: Does the keep-warm scheduler pair hold both Cloud Run services warm with min-instances at 0? Quiet window of 30+ minutes with only the pings hitting the services, then the first real requests.

jobs.taal-web-keepwarm: */10 * * * * UTC, GET web / (prerendered static page, no API call)

window: quiet from 15:20 IST (last manual request) to 15:50 IST; first requests at about 15:50 IST on follow-up deploy fbbcf0a (taal-agents-00143-8v9, taal-web-00080-72v)

instance_count.source: Cloud Monitoring run.googleapis.com/container/instance_count, 5-minute max, summed per service
instance_count.taal_agents: 2 at 15:10 to 15:15 IST (deploy overlap), then 1 in every 5-minute bucket to 15:50 IST
instance_count.taal_web: 2 at 15:10 to 15:15 IST (deploy overlap), then 1 in every 5-minute bucket to 15:50 IST

reading: Both services stayed at one instance the whole window, so the first real hit was warm: web root 0.34 s, Approve 1.65 s (no 8 to 12 s cold start).
caveat: No cold baseline was taken: taal-agents-warm already pinged every 5 minutes before this window, so taal-agents never idled to 0 and the web service got its pings from 14:28 IST. One round only. The 8 to 12 s cold start quoted elsewhere is from earlier measurements, not repeated here. instance_count includes idle instances, so it does not prove billing time.
